# Radoslav Radev Advises Never Going To Failure Every Workout

Radoslav Radev advises never going to failure every single workout, because it tires the nervous system and causes loss of progress. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 03:50]

## Details

- Pushing to the limit every session makes the nervous system more and more tired, and slowly you start losing progress. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 03:50]
- From four workouts per week for push and pull, you can push yourself to the limit maximum two workouts. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 04:31]
- The other two workouts you can train at 50 to 70 percent effort and use them to fix mistakes in technique, use a resistance band to try the next progression, or focus on something new. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 04:40]

## Evidence

- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 03:50 (Radoslav Radev): "rule number three never go to a failure every single workout it's really wrong and i know a lot of people who doing that they push themselves to the limit every single session and what happens every workout the nervous system getting more and more tired the next workout even more tired and slowly they start losing progress"
- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 04:31 (Radoslav Radev): "from four workouts per week push and pull you can push yourself to the limit maximum two workouts to do more hold more reps or to go to the next progression"
- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 04:40 (Radoslav Radev): "the other two workouts if you want you can train 50 to 70 percent effort and in these days you can use them to fix mistakes in your technique"

## Connected Ideas

- [[Radoslav Radev Advises Having A Structure To Track Results But Also Listening To Your Body]] — both rules address auto-regulation and avoiding overtraining.
- [[Radoslav Radev Recommends Active Recovery On Rest Days Instead Of Full Rest]] — active recovery supports nervous system recovery between limit sessions.
